claims: An AMBER Alert is an emergency child abduction broadcast system.
An AMBER Alert notifies the public to help locate a missing child believed to be in imminent danger.
AMBER Alerts use radio, TV, highway signs, and wireless devices to blast information about the child and suspect across a designated area.
AMBER Alert criteria generally require law enforcement to believe a child under 18 has been abducted.
AMBER Alert criteria generally require law enforcement to believe the child is in danger of serious bodily harm or death.
AMBER Alert criteria generally require enough descriptive information to help the public find the child.
AMBER Alerts are sent directly to cell phones via the Wireless Emergency Alerts program.
The AMBER Alert system has its inception in 1996.
Since its inception in 1996, the AMBER Alert system has helped safely recover over 1,290 children in the U.S.
The AMBER Alert is named for 9-year-old Amber Hagerman.
Amber Hagerman was abducted and murdered in Texas in 1996.
